findings.text: The normal task selection entry delegates to a shared picker without forcing extension work, while the server entry forces extension work but only when the extension subsystem is active, otherwise yielding no candidate.

Dispatch outcome drives selection: a retry outcome restarts the outer loop, a keep previous outcome retains the incumbent with slice replenishment when empty, otherwise the head of the local dispatch queue is taken and a missing head yields idleness.
A higher priority class becoming runnable during dispatch aborts extension selection and restarts scheduling, unless the caller explicitly forced extension selection.

Preempted runnable tasks with remaining slice stay on the local dispatch queue at its head when bypass is inactive, while tasks marked for immediate handling are returned to the scheduler with a preempted marker and cleared reason bits.

An open rescue keeps its task on the local queue even with exhausted slice, using capacity ignoring insertion and choosing head placement based on whether rescue continuation was requested, with continuation appended when preempted by peer extension work.

When the next task belongs to a class above the extension and the current task may remain on its processor, the current task is requeued with a last notification to solicit a follow up event, otherwise it is requeued without that marker.

The kick synchronization waiter releases the runqueue lock and enables interrupts while spinning on remote progress, advances its own progress marker to prevent cyclic waits, clears satisfied members from the pending set, and repeats until the set is empty.

A queued synchronization waiter that executes on a processor different from its runqueue must exit immediately because its snapshots belong to another runqueue and the targeted processors are already progressing.

Dispatch wrappers release pinning around the single dispatch step, then restore pinning and defer any pending synchronization wait to a balance callback that may sleep, avoiding deadlock with processors sending interrupts while being waited on.

Core scheduling dispatch skips work when dispatch is already in flight, runs deferred work directly when invoked for a foreign runqueue because callbacks cannot be queued remotely, and requests a retry when the dispatch step dropped the lock.
A build without core scheduling support provides a dispatch variant that always reports no work.

Runqueue selection for a waking task keeps the previous processor for execution wakeups, delegates to the scheduler selector with reentrancy guards when available and bypass is inactive, keeps the previous processor while bypassing, and otherwise uses the default idle selector with deferred default slice state on success.

Default idle selection intersects the caller restriction with task affinity using per processor scratch masks, prefers synchronous waker affinity and wholly idle sibling groups when relevant, then falls back through previous processor, siblings, locality group, node, and wider online nodes respecting idle scope flags.

Idle claiming clears the sibling group from the wholly idle set even on failure to avoid repeated attempts, with extra handling ensuring offline members are eventually cleared to prevent livelock in the search loop.

Default selection disables preemption across mask preparation and holds read side protection while consulting topology groupings, releasing in reverse order, while the multi node search additionally guards its visited set with preemption control.
A task whose allowed count reaches the possible processor count is treated as unrestricted, permitting direct use of topology group masks without intersection work.
Task extension state carries remaining slice, queue and immediacy flags, chosen processor, and deferred dispatch attributes for slice, enqueue disposition, and target queue.

Runqueue extension state carries a local dispatch queue with count and list linkage, a runnable list, online and dispatch related flags, a pending synchronization set with progress markers, and selector reentrancy state.

Affinity changes apply common handling first and stop for tasks that are dead and off processor, otherwise notify the scheduler with the effective mask when the corresponding operation exists and the task is enabled under identifier based task management.

Online transition marks the runqueue extension as online, while offline transition clears that mark, flushes rescue work, and when the processor stays active does nothing further, otherwise requeues tasks that are not already local so push logic can migrate them.
A task counts as dead and finished only when its observed state is dead and it is not currently on its processor, checked with the runqueue lock held.

A local queue head with empty slice that may remain on its processor triggers a single warning when bypass is inactive and then receives a default refill, preventing silent execution with no accounting.
Enqueue disposition distinguishes head placement, last only notification, requeue after preemption, capacity check bypass, and default slice refill, with local queue identity as a dispatch target.
Dispatch verdicts distinguish absence of work, retention of the incumbent, and retry of selection, with retry also used when higher priority activity intervenes.

Rescue continuation requires the runqueue lock held and declines when no rescue slice remains, when the task is not marked queued, or when bypass is active for its scheduler, otherwise it installs the remaining rescue slice.
A build without rescue support provides a continuation helper that always declines, preserving call compatibility while disabling the rescue path.

Task operation invocation records the target task for nested kernel helpers, warns on scheduler mismatch when nested schedulers exist and on unexpected reentrancy, then clears the record after the call.
The wake notification entry runs deferred runqueue work without further action.
The rescue continuation helper is shared across extension files with an always declining fallback for builds lacking rescue support.
The default idle processor selector is a shared helper used by the wakeup runqueue selection path.
The local queue peek returns the first queued task or absence when the local list is empty.
A build without multi node search provides a variant that always reports failure to find an idle processor.
